title: Venezuela knocks out defending WBC champ Japan with a mighty blow
content:
MIAMI — In a tournament hardly lacking in dynamic moments, monstrous home runs and epic comebacks, Saturday’s quarterfinal between Venezuela and Japan might have topped it all.

Wilyer Abreu’s towering three-run blast powered Venezuela’s 8-5 win over Japan, an upset that sends Venezuela to the World Baseball Classic semifinals for the first time since 2009. It’s the biggest victory for Venezuela in 15 years, and a devastating loss for the reigning WBC champions.

Five players homered, but no long ball was as monumental as Abreu’s. Trailing 5-4 in the top of the sixth, Abreu turned on a fastball at the top of the zone from Japan’s Hiromi Itoh.

The no-doubt shot to the upper deck in right field made it 7-5, sending the Venezuelan crowd into delirium. It was a defining moment for Abreu and for Venezuela, which has never won the World Baseball Classic.

Japan, which jumped out to a 5-2 lead in the third inning, was held scoreless for the next six frames.

Venezuela advances to Monday’s semifinal against Italy, which defeated Puerto Rico 8-6 on Sunday afternoon. The winner of Monday’s game will advance to the championship against the winner of the United States-Dominican Republic semifinal.

— This story will be updated.
